title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an identity impersonation fraud in which AI-generated images and videos were used to create a false likeness of a real, named attorney and distribute it across social media platforms. The fabricated content was used to solicit payment for immigration legal services that the real attorney never offered. The fraud operated through a chain of steps, each one outside any platform's apparent detection: synthetic media creation, mass account creation, redirection to private messaging channels, and collection of payments through peer-to-peer apps.

The failure is not located in a single AI system but in the absence of checks at multiple points where synthetic media enters public distribution. Platforms removed thousands of accounts only after an anti-piracy firm was hired to find them, meaning detection depended entirely on a private third party acting after the fact. A real person's professional reputation and likeness were used as the lure, and the targets were people seeking legal status, a population with strong reasons to trust an apparently credentialed professional and strong reasons to avoid official complaint channels.

What is not established is who is responsible for operating the scheme, whether any authority has identified or charged anyone, and whether any victim has recovered money lost.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, discovered that criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provides, charging fees ranging from $2,200 for services like US residency assistance. The fraud escalated dramatically in recent months, with potential clients calling his office after seeing the fake videos on social media platforms.

Leal's firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fraudulent accounts, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to contact phone numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal is warning immigrants to verify the identities of anyone offering legal services online and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scheme.
